prompt: A 60 kg person stands on one heel of area $1.0\ \text{cm}^{2}$. Calculate the pressure on the floor. Take $g=9.8\ \text{m s}^{-2}$.
markscheme: $P=\dfrac FA=\dfrac{60\times9.8}{1.0\times10^{-4}}$ **(M1)** $=5.9\times10^{6}$ Pa **(A1)** — far larger than under a flat shoe, which is why heels dent floors.

prompt: How many moles are in a sample containing $3.0\times10^{23}$ molecules? ($N_A=6.02\times10^{23}\ \text{mol}^{-1}$)
State three assumptions of the kinetic model of an ideal gas.
A fixed mass of gas has volume 2.0 L at 300 K and 100 kPa. It is compressed to 1.5 L and heated to 350 K. Calculate the new pressure.
markscheme:
$\dfrac{P_1V_1}{T_1}=\dfrac{P_2V_2}{T_2}\Rightarrow P_2=100\times\dfrac{2.0}{1.5}\times\dfrac{350}{300}$ **(M1)** $=156$ kPa **(A1)**

Temperatures must be in kelvin; the volume units cancel.

prompt: A cylinder of volume $0.020\ \text{m}^{3}$ contains gas at $2.0\times10^{5}$ Pa and 20 °C. Calculate the amount of gas and the number of molecules. ($R=8.31\ \text{J mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$, $N_A=6.02\times10^{23}\ \text{mol}^{-1}$)

**(a)** Explain how the motion of gas molecules produces a pressure on the walls of a container. **[2]**

**(b)** Air at $1.0\times10^{5}$ Pa has density $1.2\ \text{kg m}^{-3}$. Use $P=\tfrac13\rho\overline{v^{2}}$ to estimate the root-mean-square speed of its molecules. **[1]**
markscheme:
**(a)** Each molecule that rebounds from a wall has its momentum changed, so the wall exerts a force on it and (Newton's third law) it exerts a force on the wall **(R1)**; the many collisions per second produce an average force per unit area — pressure **(R1)**

**(b)** $v_{rms}=\sqrt{\dfrac{3P}{\rho}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{3\times1.0\times10^{5}}{1.2}}=500\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ **(A1)**

concept: Internal energy of an ideal monatomic gas
prompt: Calculate the internal energy of 2.0 mol of helium (an ideal monatomic gas) at 300 K, and explain why it contains no potential energy term.
markscheme:
$U=\tfrac32nRT=1.5\times2.0\times8.31\times300=7.5\times10^{3}$ J **(A1)**

Ideal gas molecules exert no forces on each other between collisions, so there is no intermolecular potential energy **(R1)**

prompt: A real gas behaves most like an ideal gas at:
markscheme: **D.** At low pressure (low density) molecules are far apart, so their own volume and intermolecular forces matter little; at high temperature their kinetic energy greatly exceeds any intermolecular potential energy.
